findings.summary: Export scope does not match the contract's IN-06 git bound that the node's own constraint defers to ('scope of repos and history depth is exactly what the evidence contract names'). The contract (part2/contract/evidence-contract.md, IN-06, labeled (06)) requires including a commit ONLY if it touches .handoffs/, project-docs/, 01-decisions/, 02-corpus/, 03-ingestion/, 04-evaluation/, AGENTS.md, PROJECT-BRIEF.md, gddp/, graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md, is cited in admitted decision git_refs[], or falls in the Node-10 dated window — and explicitly says 'No full-clone dump.' The delivered export dumps ALL 164 commits; 102 of 164 touch no IN-06 path (context-refinery/, scratch/, .gddp/ gate tokens, api/, deploy/, etc.). The export also carries no IN-06 inclusion markers, so the bounded set is not identifiable downstream.

Change evidence is partial relative to the contract: export carries per-file numstat (stat-like: lines_added/lines_deleted, binary|text status) but no change_evidence.diff at all, whereas IN-06 requires 'Always emit change_evidence.stat' AND 'Emit change_evidence.diff only for those commits, bounded and truncated if clipped.' The git class extras in the contract (change_evidence.{stat,diff,truncated}) cannot be satisfied from this artifact alone.

Reproducibility guarantee is not fully delivered: the script is deterministic given a fixed HEAD but has no HEAD-pinning guard, and the sha256 is only printed to stdout — no persisted hash artifact in part2/layers/git/. The export was generated at head 131a143 (164 commits); the wrapper commit 0fbcb09 (which adds the export files themselves) is already in history, so a naive re-run at the current HEAD produces a 165-record file that is NOT byte-identical to the recorded export. The docstring documents this caveat honestly, but the 'recorded sha256 matches on rebuild' property that the reproducible criterion (and node-09's deterministic-rebuild check) relies on is not verifiable from the artifact set as delivered.

The delivered artifact is a full-history unfiltered dump (102/164 commits touch no IN-06 path) with numstat-only change evidence and no diff field, and the reproducibility property is only conditional (HEAD not pinned; sha256 printed but not recorded as an artifact; re-run at current HEAD yields 165 records vs the recorded 164). These are subtle but real veers from the node's intended role as bounded by its own constraints — drift, not block: the files are at the required path, the format is consumable, and downstream can recover (node-08 can apply IN-06 filtering when materializing corpus items; node-09 can pin HEAD to the recorded head_commit at rebuild). Graph structure and dependency placement are intact (node-06→08→09→13/15/16 chain is sound), so graph integrity at the structural level is preserved; the risks are forward-looking and carried as observations. A human should look because the over-inclusive export and non-persisted hash directly affect the next node's (08/09) ability to pass contract inclusion and deterministic-rebuild checks.

import hashlib, json, subprocess
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path("part2/layers/git/git-export.jsonl")
HEAD_PIN = "131a143fa0bfa4151645a29fedb80f99c7df1055"  # head recorded in the export manifest
REC_SEP = "\x1e"; END_SEP = "\x1f"
COMMIT_FMT = REC_SEP.join(["%H","%P","%at","%ct","%aN","%cN"]) + REC_SEP + "%B" + END_SEP

def git(*args):
    r = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0: raise RuntimeError(r.stderr.strip())
    return r.stdout

def iso_utc(unix):
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(unix), tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

The recorded sha256 (b3ae90b0..., in commit 0fbcb09's message) matches the shipped artifact. Two issues need human attention, one of which is a direct criterion failure: (1) REPRODUCIBILITY: a faithful re-run of the saved script at the manifest's pinned head (131a143fa) does NOT produce byte-identical output — rebuilt sha256 is 2551e0c7... vs recorded b3ae90b0...; 9 of 164 entries differ, exclusively in numstat lines_added/lines_deleted counts. Direct git invocations confirm git 2.54.0 in this environment yields different counts than the file records for the same commits (e.g., 69/6 vs 70/7; 1418822/657 vs 1418909/744). The output is sensitive to git version/config (diff algorithm, rename detection), which the script does not pin, so 'byte-identical on rebuild' does not hold here even though it may have held on the executor's machine at build time. (2) SCOPE NUANCE (not a criterion failure): the export is full history while contract IN-06 bounds inclusion to commits touching listed paths/cited in git_refs/dated window, and IN-06's change_evidence.diff (bounded/truncated) is not present in the raw export — stat is emitted, diff appears deferred to node-08 layer build. Dates fully satisfy the absolute ISO-8601 requirement. Verdict: criterion 1 pass, criterion 2 fail as measured, criterion 3 pass; flagged for human confirmation because the criterion-2 failure is environment-sensitive and the recorded sha does match the shipped artifact.
